name: Schema Design Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in schema design work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in schema design work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple schema design strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to schema design (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. Validate schema design outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
4. Document any non-obvious schema design decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen schema design approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. When schema design guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
7. Prefer the simplest schema design approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
8. When schema design decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
9. State assumptions about schema design explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
10. Prefer explicit, readable schema design solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
11. Check that schema design terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
12. Measure before optimizing any schema design bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated schema design concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new schema design abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of schema design correctness.
- Do not skip documenting schema design assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about schema design over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
